summary: SL-100 fixed the dead Ctrl+Enter after a live refresh by restoring selection and focus by Path. It does this in MainWindow.ShowTopLevel (MainWindow.xaml.cs:379-439): the Ordinal reselect is synchronous right after the ItemsSource swap, and the refocus runs in the existing Loaded callback. Items stay TopLevelRow, containers still detach, and Q-078 left the keep-containers-alive work (Derived 1 and 5) unbuilt. The product change is one function, but the slice added 28 Facts, a 12-row focus-return corpus, a hook top-key step, R-001 step 16 and a fitness exemption. The repro and 28 new Facts pass, validate's guards are green, and the real-exe hook step passes 3 of 3. The person-run Explorer reveal, SC-181's by-hand clicks and a real Alt+Tab were not reached.

payload.reason: The follow-up budget is full (31 open, ceiling 30) and SL-100 is itself a follow-up of the SL-047 reflection, so no candidates are raised. What this slice deferred is already filed: SC-263 (SelectedItem fallback), SC-264 (partly visible row scroll), SC-265 (unread `gap` flag), SC-266 (modal-dialog hang), plus the design's filed_for_later items (standing guard, keep-containers-alive).
payload.estimate_error: Size 'medium' was about right, but the work sat in the wrong place. The product diff is one function in one src file (MainWindow.xaml.cs). The rest of the 15 changed files (the build stage's list names 10 of them) are tests, the hook, WindowCases.ps1, fitness.yaml, ArchitectureRulesTests.cs and a doc. The design's "about 25 lines" described the least of the work. Risk 'low' was too low. Lessons #337 and #186 already said not to tier MainWindow row and gesture slices low. The slice then drew two critique rounds and two code-review rounds, the build widened the design's focus trigger (FocusIsAdrift), and the fitness.yaml edit added the 124-row rules harness to validate. Validate came to roughly 35 minutes of runs: WindowMutants 408 s, L-001/2/3 at 30+85+88 s, rules harness, default suite and publish. No finding was above minor and nothing shipped broken, so the error was under-tiering, not harm.

learned.lesson: Size a WPF row or gesture fix in this app by its test and window-hook surface, not by the MainWindow diff. Here the product change is one function (ShowTopLevel, MainWindow.xaml.cs:379-439). The cost was 28 Facts plus a 12-row corpus, a RevealMode top-key step, R-001 step 16, and a fitness.yaml/ArchitectureRulesTests edit that dragged in the all-scenario rules harness. Budget validate at 35+ minutes for any slice that touches MainWindow.xaml.cs and WindowCases.ps1 together.
learned.evidence: build-slice file list: 1 file in src/FsAnalyser.App and 10 test, hook, rule and doc files. validate: WindowMutants -Mutant All 408 s, L-001/L-002/L-003 30/85/88 s, rules harness 124 of 124, default suite 804 of 805.

learned.lesson: Do not encode a focus-capture condition from memory. Measure where WPF puts keyboard focus first. The design and critique assumed that a closed row menu or a re-activated window leaves an active window with null focus. Both actually leave focus on MainWindow itself, so the repair trigger had to become FocusIsAdrift (MainWindow.xaml.cs:422-423), which is wider than Q-078's 'if the list had keyboard focus'. A refresh now also moves a focus left on the window's blank area onto the selected row. Start any further focus work from tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh/FocusReturnCorpus.json (F01-F12) and FocusReturnTests.cs, not from the recalled model.
learned.evidence: build-slice deviation list; FocusReturnTests.cs:188 asserts `Keyboard.FocusedElement is Window` after reactivation; corpus row F11 expects focus to be taken, the opposite of the design's case 8.

learned.lesson: The SL-100 Rig swallows dispatcher exceptions. Its Dispatcher.UnhandledException handler marks everything Handled (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:361-365), and ModalDialogAround (FocusReturnTests.cs:236-241) runs `whileOpen(); dialog.Close();` with no try/finally. A throw inside ShowTopLevel while a modal dialog is open therefore hangs corpus rows F07 and F08, and with them the acceptance command. Until SC-266 is built, run the SL-100 project with --blame-hang-timeout. Anyone reusing the Rig inherits the same hang.
learned.evidence: code-review round 2 reproduced it: ShowTopLevel mutated to throw only while MainWindow owns a window, F01 passed, F07 hung until --blame-hang-timeout 45s killed the testhost ('Test Run Aborted').

learned.lesson: The restore has no standing guard. tests/bugs/* projects sit outside FsAnalyser.slnx, so the default suite never runs them. WindowMutants -Mutant All, which Q-114 requires for any App diff, passed all 12 mutants with no mutant that touches focus or selection across a refresh. A later ShowTopLevel rewrite can drop the restore with every required check green. Keep the SL-100 project and its pre-fix SHA 7bf476e in view for the next slice that edits ShowTopLevel, and name the SL-100 acceptance command in that slice's validate guards.
learned.evidence: critique m4 (deferred), design filed_for_later 'standing guard', validate: 12 of 12 mutants caught while M0 (pre-fix MainWindow) went 24 of 29 red only in the SL-100 project.

learned.lesson: Builder scratch files in the worktree reach the default suite. The untracked .taad-scratch/sl100-topkey-run.ps1 turned AppArgumentTests red (804 of 805) at validate, and validate had to move it aside to show the committed tree is green. Keep scratch out of the repo tree, or delete it before the build stage ends. Mutant recipes must pin the pre-fix commit, not HEAD: sl100-mutants.ps1 builds M0 from `git show HEAD:`, so since 0e43204 it resolves to the fixed file and 'M0 24 of 29 red' cannot be reproduced from it.
learned.evidence: validate-slice default-suite result and its AppArgumentTests rerun; code-review round 1 drift note on the scratch M0 script.

learned.lesson: When tests are the main body of work (lesson #176), tell the first code-review pass to read the test harness's failure paths: swallowed exceptions, hangs, and flags no code reads. Pass 1 checked the production fix and the 14-row matrix against the design and passed. Both test-infrastructure defects (the ModalDialogAround hang and the unread corpus `gap` flag) surfaced only in the adversarial second round. All 12 findings in this slice (8 critique, 4 code-review) were disposed by a model with no person triage, so the gates' precision is still unmeasured.
learned.evidence: code-review #1 halted, #2 found R2-m3 and R2-m4. Critique #2 and code-review #2 both report 'answered by a model, counted as untriaged'.

learned.lesson: Reconcile a contract with the outside claims that contradict it. The design's contract and doc said 'the restore never scrolls', while its own recalled outside claim said Focus() can shift the offset by up to one row for a partly visible row. Nobody forced the exception into the contract, and it went unstated except in a test comment (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:106). It is now SC-264. When a design lists a 'recalled' claim that would falsify a contract line, the critique should require the exception in the contract or a Fact for it.
learned.evidence: code-review R1-m2; docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:27; O-023 waived to SC-264.

learned.lesson: SC-263 (resolve SelectedItem in OnCanOpenInExplorer/OnOpenInExplorer) must key on MainWindow.FocusIsAdrift (MainWindow.xaml.cs:422-423), not on 'focus is TopLevelList'. Corpus rows F02, F05 and F08 pin focus on the Window, so a list-only fallback leaves them dead. The wrong wording is in docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:78-80, in FocusReturnCorpus.json bounded_by and in the filed follow-up. O-022 waived the correction to SC-263 instead of rewording the three lines, so check them when SC-263 opens.
learned.evidence: code-review R1-m1 ('accepted-pending'), then O-022 waived; FocusReturnTests.cs:188 and :164.

learned.lesson: The keep-containers-alive direction is closed until a row action needs it (Q-078). The reflection's 'diff the list' idea was model-derived, and two no-go spikes confirmed Q-078: Move of the focused ListBoxItem disconnects its container (S3 0/10, S4 3/10), and the real MainWindow lost it at refresh r3. Derived 1 and 5 stay unmet by decision, and the Tag/CommandTarget=Window pattern (lesson #187) still applies to every new row action. If it is ever built, start from spike 1's 'fixsafe' variant (move the other rows past the focused one, 40 of 40 on a stand-in) and unwrap Current in four readers: the SL-100 repro, the SL-063 tests, WindowReport.cs:247 and the hook.
learned.evidence: risk-spike #1 (experiments 1 and 2 no-go, 3 go at 240/240); design key_decisions; Q-078.

learned.lesson: A leftover 'run it on net10.0-windows' check (SC-181) was already satisfied before the slice. Directory.Build.props:4 has targeted net10.0-windows since SL-020 (d1f97b7), and SL-047's probe was a net10 run. Close such leftovers by reading the TargetFramework history before merging them into a bug slice. What SC-181 still owes is a person's real clicks and a real Alt+Tab.
learned.evidence: investigation 'Ruled out' entry; build-check criterion 6 (checked_by person); validate 'not reached' list.

lessons_judged.why: The design kept OnRowContextMenuOpened's Tag/CommandTarget=Window pattern unchanged and added AnOpenRowMenuSurvivesARefresh, so the refocus never steals focus from an open row menu.
The slice adds no per-row marks, so whether top-level rows are visible after a Completed scan did not bear on the focus and selection restore.
The restore's stale-array guard compares TopLevelList.ItemsSource against the assigned array with ReferenceEquals. The snapshot channel and Core were left untouched.

The extra layout and refocus run inside _refreshClock so the SlowRefresh skip still sees their cost. A 100,000-row probe gave a median refresh of 25.8 ms with the restore against 22.4 ms without, and L-002 passed.
The timer and StartScan-finally facts were not needed. The only touch was ShowFinalTopLevel racing the tick's Loaded callback, which was read directly from the code.

Nothing in this slice was a critique claim about scan-end or hook-mode lifecycle that proved wrong because the stack line lagged. The wrong recalled claim here was about WPF focus landing, which is a different failure.

The top-key step was added inside the existing reveal mode, with no new FSA_HOOK_MODE value, as the lesson prescribes. It was run on the published exe over a Hidden-folder tree with FSA_HOOK_EXPLORER_VIEW=0|0.
It held again: one src file changed against 10 test, hook, rule and doc files (per the build stage's file list). Hook and case work drove the cost, and the validate runs followed from it.
Validate published the exe with eng/dotnet.ps1 publish and ran L-001, L-002 and L-003 plus the top-key hook step against it. The Core tests alone would not have exercised the window.
Validate budgeted for it and ran WindowMutants -Mutant All (408 s) and the rules harness with all scenarios, because WindowCases.ps1, fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs changed.
The design filed the network pass for a person and made no cancel-safety claim for the stalled share. The slice touched MainWindow and the FsaWindowHook, which is what renews the debt.
Every build, test, publish and mutant run went through eng/dotnet.ps1 on SDK 10.0.401 and produced net10.0-windows output.

missed.what: Finding m7 prescribed the repair branch `window.IsActive && Keyboard.FocusedElement is null && selectedKey != null`, and m8 prescribed a list-only SelectedItem fallback. Both rested on a recalled claim that a closed row menu or a re-activated window leaves an active window with null focus. The critique never asked to measure where focus lands before prescribing a condition. The build measured that both leave focus on MainWindow itself. The trigger had to become FocusIsAdrift (MainWindow.xaml.cs:422-423), wider than Q-078's scope, and m8's list-only form would not repair corpus rows F02, F05 or F08. A check: any critique finding that prescribes a Keyboard.FocusedElement condition must name the Fact that measures it.
missed.caught_by: build (FocusReturnTests.cs:164 and :188 measured Window, not null); code review round 1 caught the m8 wording

missed.what: The design declared no architecture rules and no fitness impact. The repro file already on disk, and the Press technique every new Fact reuses (Ctrl set in the thread key state), add user32 DllImports under tests/. ArchitectureRulesTests.InteropLivesOnlyInNative and both fitness.yaml entries for that rule went red. The fix needed except_files entries for tests/bugs/SL-100-ResultsListRefresh/** and RevealMode.cs, and the fitness.yaml edit then forced the full 124-row rules harness (Q-026/Q-027) at validate. The critique did not ask which existing fitness rules the new test project's P/Invokes would hit.
missed.caught_by: build (architecture rule tests red once the SL-100 tree was on disk)

missed.what: The design ordered the callback as scroll restore, then UpdateLayout, then ContainerFromItem, with a stale-array guard. It justified this with the recalled claim that realised containers belong to the pre-restore offset after the Reset. The build measured that the swap leaves the offset and containers in place by Loaded. UpdateLayout and the guard are unobservable (mutants M3 and M4 survive) and were kept only because the design said so. The critique accepted the recalled claim without asking for a Fact that fails without UpdateLayout.

The design's contract and key decision say 'the restore never scrolls'. Its own outside_claims entry (recalled) says Focus() can shift the offset by up to one item for a partly visible row. The critique did not force the contract to state the one-row exception or require a Fact for the cut-off last slot. The doc shipped with the unqualified claim (docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:27) and only a test comment (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:106) admits it.

Round 1 did not read the test harness's failure paths. Rig.ModalDialogAround (FocusReturnTests.cs:236-241) has no try/finally, and the Rig's UnhandledException handler marks every exception Handled (ResultsListShapeTests.cs:361-365). A throw in ShowTopLevel while the modal dialog is open skips dialog.Close(), so corpus rows F07 and F08 hang the acceptance command instead of failing it.
missed.caught_by: code-review round 2 (reproduced with --blame-hang-timeout 45s; waived to SC-266)

missed.what: Round 1 passed the corpus without noticing that the `gap` flag on F02, F05 and F08 is read by no code, and TheCorpusUsesOnlyTheWordsItDefines does not tie it to `expect: press-dead`. A new dead Ctrl+Enter can be pinned as expected behaviour without being declared a gap. A check: assert per row that gap equals (expect == 'press-dead').

unknowns: Does a real Alt+Tab, or Explorer taking the foreground after Ctrl+Enter, leave focus on MainWindow itself, as the in-process SetActiveWindow/SetFocus simulation measured? The corpus rows F02 and F05 depend on it. Only a person's SC-181 run can answer it.

Does a real hardware Ctrl+Enter whose WM_KEYDOWN lands between a tick's ItemsSource swap and its Loaded callback run after the restore (SC-254)? Every press so far was raised in-process, and the Input-priority ordering was shown only by Facts and spike 3.

Does the wider FocusIsAdrift trigger take focus in any real flow the Facts do not cover, such as a person who clicks blank window area mid-scan on a real C:\ or D:\ scan? The published exe ran only on a synthetic 48,000-folder tree under %LOCALAPPDATA%\Temp.

Does container.Focus() scroll the list by one row when the focused row sits partly visible in the viewport's last slot? No test pins it (SC-264). It is ordinary during a live scan, because the focused row's index changes with every resize.

Does R-001 step 16 pass in a real person run that opens Explorer? Neither the step nor the real reveal after Ctrl+Enter has ever been executed, and lesson #340 says each WindowCases.ps1 edit draws a new finding.
what_went_wrong: The design's recalled claim that menu-close and reactivation leave null focus was wrong. The build measured the Window itself and widened the restore trigger beyond Q-078's 'if the list had keyboard focus'. Only a model accepted that behaviour change (a refresh now takes a focus left on the window's blank area), and no person decided it.

The recorded m8 follow-up named the wrong focus state in three places: the doc (docs/design/SL-100-results-list-refresh.md:78-80), the corpus bounded_by text and the builder's follow-up. Code review had to correct it, and the correction was waived to SC-263 instead of rewording three lines, so the wrong text is probably still in the shipped doc and corpus.

Three code-review findings of real size were waived to the backlog: the unstated scroll exception (SC-264), the unread `gap` flag (SC-265) and the modal-dialog hang (SC-266). The shipped state includes a doc claim ('the refresh never scrolls') known to be false by one row, and an acceptance command that can hang if ShowTopLevel throws.
Code review needed two rounds. The first passed the production fix and matrix but missed the test-Rig hang and the unread corpus flag. The adversarial second round found both and reproduced the hang.

The design kept two pieces nothing can observe: the stale-array guard and UpdateLayout (mutants M3 and M4 survive), because its case-5 premise (containers belong to the pre-restore offset) did not hold in the harness. They are carried as unverified code.

The design declared no architecture rules, yet the interop rule went red once the SL-100 tree was on disk. The fix touched fitness.yaml and ArchitectureRulesTests.cs, which added the all-scenario rules harness (124 rows) to validate.

The default suite was 804 of 805 at validate because the builder's untracked scratch launcher (.taad-scratch/sl100-topkey-run.ps1) tripped AppArgumentTests. The builder's mutant script now resolves M0 to the fixed file, so the recorded 'M0 24 of 29 red' cannot be reproduced from it.

The headline merged criterion (SC-181, real clicks against a live refresh) and the requested Q-078 window case (R-001 step 16, with a real Explorer reveal) were not run by anything. The only evidence is in-process Facts and a refusal-only hook run, and all 12 findings had only model triage.
